summary: Something work needs to get done: a role someone fills, an outside partner, a system or a place.
example: Data analyst (a role), analytics partner (an outside partner), handheld scanner (a system), cold store (a place).
definition: A resource is what a project, programme or operation draws on to do its work: a role somebody fills, an organisational unit, an external party, a system, a facility or a governance body that decides on it. It is declared once in the Resource catalogue and picked wherever it is needed: in a project's resources, as the owner of a goal, objective or outcome, as a programme's sponsor, as an operation's service owner, on a stakeholder map, and as the holder of a budget. A resource names a role or a thing, never a person: people are principals who sign in and hold roles, and no definition names them (TAXONOMY.md D27). A budget is not a resource: money is what the work draws on to pay for the work, and it is a funding source, with its own code, holder and period (TAXONOMY.md D7). An organisational unit here is one the work draws on; the teams that carry work and keep definitions are the Team kind.

/metadata/name.guide: The standard name of the role or thing, as anyone in the organisation would say it. A role is named for the position, so it stays true when the person in it changes. Names are unique in the catalogue, so reuse an entry before adding one.

poor.why: A person, not a role: Cartograph names roles, and people hold them. Name the position she fills, such as Operations lead.
Money, not a resource: a budget is a funding source, with a code, a holder and a period (TAXONOMY.md D7). Define it as a budget and name it on the project's funding.

poor.text: Depot supervisor at the north depot
poor.why: One post, not a role: the catalogue holds the role once, and a project says where it needs it.
An activity, not something the work draws on: the training is work in a project; the role that runs it is the Training facilitator.
A slice of what you serve, which is a segment: you compare measures across it. A resource is something the work draws on to get done, such as the Regional coordinator who works there.

/spec/category.guide: What kind of resource this is: a role (personRole), an organisational unit (orgUnit), an external party (externalParty), a system, a facility, a governance body (governanceBody), or other. Pick the one that says what the work draws on. A governance body is a committee or board that decides: it confirms success, receives escalations and issues decisions, named once here and referenced wherever it is. Other is for the rare case none fits; when other starts to fill up, the catalogue is holding something that belongs elsewhere.

poor.why: Chosen for a budget such as the Seasonal training budget. Money is a funding source, not a resource, so it belongs in Budgets, not under other (TAXONOMY.md D7).
Chosen for the Transport contractor. A contracted haulier is outside the organisation, so it is an external party.
Chosen for the steering committee. A committee decides rather than does the work, so it is a governance body; it is not a Team either, since a team owns work and scopes who may edit it.

/spec/description.guide: What the role does or what the thing is for, in one sentence, so someone choosing from the catalogue can tell it from its neighbours. Up to 240 characters. Say the work, not who does it today.
good: Runs one depot day to day, including intake and the quality check.
The scanner used at intake to record a delivery against a member.
Contracted haulier moving produce between depots and retail partners.

poor.text: Ada, who has run the north depot since 2019.
poor.why: Describes a person and her history, not the role: when she moves on, the entry is wrong.
Says nothing a reader could use to tell this entry from any other.
